title: Ethanol + water + ethyl acetate, UNIQUAC, 35 stages: CHEPTA-Lab's product column 11 without acetic acid
purpose: Proposal 0024, test 3: CHEPTA-Lab's column 11 of the ethyl acetate plant (public repository FaireDose/CHEPTA-Lab, cases/ethyl-acetate-piotrowski-2021, input results-chepta-0.6.2/iso-scds11-acid0-bottoms141.5.request.json: the paper's feed 13 without its 0.01 mass % of acetic acid, R/D 3, product 141.5 kmol/h). Lab's input gives the feed in kg/h (ethanol 508.0404, water 1283.758, ethyl acetate 25519.4702) at 344.15 K and 100 kPa; flow_mol_s and z here are those kg/h with CHEPTA's molar masses (46.06844, 18.01528, 88.10512 g/mol). The feed is part vapour at its temperature. Two liquids on stages 1 to 30 (the ethyl acetate-water split above the feed and below it). The ethyl acetate + water + ethanol system and UNIQUAC are Lab's choice. The column with the acid (dimerizing vapour) is tested in test/columns-lab-requests.test.js; the reference has no chemical theory, so it checks this column without the acid.
method_choice: CHEPTA-Lab's: UNIQUAC with the default sets, ideal-gas vapour (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids possible: an activity model).

behaviour: two liquids on the stages the reference names (fixture columns-vll-three-phase.json)
expected.branch: The engine's solution (continuation in the relative volatilities); the reference solves its own equations from the engine's profile, perturbed.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: one-liquid stages: no trial liquid on a grid has a tangent-plane distance below -1e-9

agreement_with_data.note: The three NRTL sets are fitted to vapour-liquid data; their liquid-liquid split is W1's work (joint fits, M2b) and not a test of the column.
